questions.question: In a chemical reaction, what name is given to the starting chemicals that react together?
options: Catalysts
Products
Reactants
Solvents

questions.question: What are the newly formed chemical substances produced at the end of a chemical reaction called?
options: Reactants
Elements
Catalysts
Products

questions.question: When comparing the reactants and the products of a chemical reaction, what is true about the atoms they contain?
options: Some atoms are destroyed and new ones are created.
They contain exactly the same atoms.
The products contain more atoms than the reactants.
The reactants contain heavier atoms than the products.

questions.question: Although the same atoms exist before and after a chemical reaction, how do the products differ from the reactants?
options: The atoms in the products are bonded differently compared to the reactants.
The atoms in the products are much larger than in the reactants.
The atoms in the products have been turned into different elements.
The atoms in the products lose their mass completely.

questions.question: Which statement describes John Dalton's model of the atom?
options: A sphere that can be split into smaller negative particles
A cloud of positive charge containing tiny electrons
A central nucleus surrounded by orbiting shells
A solid sphere that cannot be broken up

questions.question: What defines a substance as being an element?
options: It is made up of only one type of atom.
It contains at least two different types of atoms bonded together.
It can easily be broken down into simpler substances by heating.
It is always a mixture of metals and non-metals.

questions.question: What do the subscript numbers next to the chemical symbols in a formula represent?
options: The melting point of the compound
The number of electrons each atom has
The number of each type of atom present in the compound
The total mass of the compound in grams

questions.question: Carbon dioxide (CO2) and carbon monoxide (CO) are different compounds. How do their chemical makeups compare?
options: They contain different elements in the same ratio.
They contain the same elements, but in a different ratio.
CO2 is a mixture of elements and CO is a single element.
They have completely different elements and no atoms in common.

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of metalloid elements?
options: They have only the properties of highly reactive metals.
They have some properties of metals and some properties of non-metals.
They are always gases at room temperature.
They do not conduct heat or electricity under any conditions.

questions.question: How do the properties of a compound compare to the properties of the elements that reacted to make it?
options: A compound always has the exact average properties of its elements.
A compound must be a gas if its elements were solids.
A compound may have completely different properties to its constituent elements.
A compound keeps the identical physical and chemical properties of each element.

questions.question: Which non-metal is unusual because it is an excellent conductor of both electricity and heat?
options: Sulfur
Graphite
Helium
Phosphorus

questions.question: How are metals and non-metals arranged on the periodic table?
options: Metals are on the right side; non-metals are on the left side and middle.
Metals are in the top row; non-metals are in the bottom row.
Metals are in the middle and on the left; non-metals are on the right side.
Metals and non-metals are scattered randomly with no clear sides.

questions.question: What is meant when a non-metal element is described as forming 'diatomic molecules'?
options: Its molecules contain exactly two atoms bonded together.
It cannot react with any other elements.
Its atoms are split into two halves.
It only exists as a liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: What ending is given to the name of a simple compound made of a metal and a non-metal to show they have bonded?
options: -ate
-ide
-ite
-ic

questions.question: What is the name given to a group of compounds that consist of metal atoms bonded to a -CO3 group?
options: Metal sulfates
Metal nitrates
Metal carbonates
Metal oxides

questions.question: What type of compound is formed when metal atoms are chemically bonded to a -SO4 group?
options: Metal sulfates
Metal carbonates
Metal nitrates
Metal hydroxides
